business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Media Relations and Crisis Public Relations Agency

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law system with Islamic Sharia as a principal source of legislation under Constitution Art. 2)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt–United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force)
Egypt–United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force)
Egypt–China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (in force)
Arab Free Trade Area / Greater Arab Free Trade Area (GAFTA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Laws No. 4/2009, 94/2015 and 158/2020) arts. 102–121; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2310 of 2017); Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorist Financing Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended by Laws No. 8/2013, 36/2014 and 154/2020) and Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 140 of 2003, as amended); Commercial Registration Law No. 34 of 1976; GAFI beneficial-owner disclosure implementing rules as applied through the GAFI e-portal and Ministerial Decree No. 208 of 2020; Central Bank of Egypt KYC and AML circulars imposing mandatory UBO identification at the 25% threshold.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incorporation of each corporate shareholder/UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registry or competent corporate authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Egypt is a Hague Apostille Convention state as of 2022) followed by certified Arabic translation and notarization in Egypt; consular legalization alternative if origin state is not a Convention party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Egyptian incorporation counsel or founding signatory to execute incorporation filings and banking onboarding
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the principal's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille followed by certified Arabic translation; if the origin state is not a Convention party, Egyptian consular legalization is mandatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of each corporate shareholder authorizing the formation of the Egyptian LLC and designating its director(s)/representative(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization plus certified Arabic translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential/business address of all directors, shareholders, authorized signatories and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public, issuing government authority, or licensed embassy/consulate in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copies apostilled or consular-legalized, followed by certified Arabic translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Banking reference or evidence of clean financial standing for each UBO where requested by the onboarding bank (retainer ACH/wire payment rail confirmation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank or financial institution of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original or apostilled/consular-legalized banker's letter with certified Arabic translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and continuous screening of every director, shareholder, authorized signatory and 25%+ UBO against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists (including Resolutions 1267/1989 and 1988), EU consolidated sanctions list, and Egypt's domestic terrorism and money-laundering lists maintained by the Egyptian Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing Unit (EMLCU) and the Central Bank of Egypt. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) and senior-management approval are required for any Politically Exposed Person (PEP), family member or close associate; adverse-media checks, source-of-wealth verification and corroborating corporate documentation are mandatory. A negative screening result must be documented in the AML/KYC file prior to incorporation and bank onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones) One-Stop-Shop e-services portal and the Egyptian Commercial Registry electronic system (www.gafi.gov.eg)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name must be in Arabic script and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any name previously reserved or registered in the Egyptian Commercial Registry. A Latin (English or French) transliteration may be recorded as an auxiliary trade name for foreign correspondence. The Arabic name must reflect or be compatible with the declared business purpose and must contain an appropriate legal form indicator (e.g., 'LLC' or 'Sharka') and, where applicable, the activity descriptor for media relations and public relations consultancy.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 days of a rejection notice, the applicant or its registered legal counsel may file a written reconsideration request with the GAFI Commercial Registration Committee, attaching a memorandum of comparison distinguishing the proposed name from existing registrations and evidencing any trademark or trade-name priority, together with supporting apostilled/consularized documents as applicable. If GAFI confirms the rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal before the State Council's Administrative Judiciary Court in accordance with Law No. 47 of 1972 on the State Council; the appeal must be lodged within 60 days of the final administrative decision. A parallel fresh name reservation with a modified name may be filed without prejudice to the pending appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not accepted as the sole statutory registered office for an Egyptian LLC. A physical Egyptian address evidenced by a notarized lease agreement, usufruct deed, title deed, or an enforceable serviced-office/coworking agreement issued by a licensed business center is mandatory for GAFI registration, commercial registry entry, tax card / Economic Identification Number (EIN) issuance, and bank account opening. Virtual telephony and remote administrative support may be layered onto the physical address but cannot replace it.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate (estimated 30–40%). GAFI and the Commercial Registry Office may conduct unannounced inspections to verify the existence and suitability of the registered office; the Egyptian Tax Authority and labor inspectors may similarly perform ad-hoc site visits. The risk is partially mitigated for a low-risk ISIC 7310 PR-services firm but remains material enough to require a genuine physical presence and accessible corporate records.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name clearance and reservation fee (Arabic corporate name) at GAFI One-Stop-Shop
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff published by GAFI for name reservation services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: LLC commercial registration and foundation filing fee at the Egyptian Commercial Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory commercial registration fee schedule under Law No. 34 of 1976 and GAFI unified fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of memorandum of association (MoA) and founding minutes before the Egyptian notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian Notary Public Authority (affiliated to the Ministry of Justice)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary fee tariff set by the Ministry of Justice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Stamp duties and official stamp fees on the memorandum of association and incorporation instruments
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Stamp Duty Law No. 111 of 1980 statutory rates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory publication of the incorporation announcement in the Official Gazette (Al-Waqa'i Al-Masriya)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication fee as required by the Companies Law for LLC founding notice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of foreign corporate documents (per set of five documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Home-country competent authority for apostille or Egyptian consulate/embassy for consular legalization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document statutory fee or prevailing official tariff in the origin country plus Egyptian consular fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Arabic translation and notarization of apostilled/legalized foreign corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Accredited official translator / Egyptian notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for certified legal translation and notarial attestation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register initial disclosure filing (details of shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: GAFI statutory filing fee for UBO data submission

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Egyptian legal counsel fees for pre-incorporation due diligence, drafting of MoA and corporate KYC/AML pack
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for LLC incorporation and compliance onboarding in Egypt (fixed-fee professional services)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018 and Law No. 152 of 2020), Articles 30–50 (Limited Liability Companies); Executive Regulations of Ministerial Decree No. 5122 of 1981; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 (Article 15 One-Stop Shop); Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976; VAT Law No. 67 of 2016.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – One-Stop Shop (OSS), with integrated Commercial Registry filing under the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade and notarization by the Egyptian Notary Public.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Contract of Incorporation and Articles of Association (AOA) executed in Arabic before an Egyptian notary public, with certified English transcript for foreign quotaholders.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an LLC under the amended Companies Law; capital is fixed by the AOA. The declared paid-up capital must be deposited in an Egyptian licensed bank, which issues a capital deposit certificate submitted with the GAFI incorporation file. Funds remain in the LLC's pre-registration bank account and are released upon issuance of the Commercial Registry certificate; no separate escrow or trust arrangement is statutorily imposed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) the quota share allocation set forth in the Articles of Association is accepted, and the paid-up capital evidenced by bank deposit certificate No. [●] issued by [●] Bank is ratified as fully paid; (2) the registered office is established at [●] Cairo, Egypt, and the General Manager is authorized to finalize the lease and register the address; (3) [Name] is appointed General Manager, [Name] Corporate Secretary, and [Name] Compliance Officer under Law No. 159 of 1981, all empowered to represent the Company before GAFI, the Commercial Registry, the Egyptian Tax Authority, and the National Organization for Social Insurance; (4) the Secretary is instructed to file this resolution and the relevant forms as attachments to the GAFI application file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Legal Status Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (OSS) — online portal 'Egypt for Investment' (investinegypt.gov.eg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed names (Arabic and Latin script) with the intended ISIC 7310 PR-communication scope; obtain the name reservation certificate and verify that the activity is permitted for 100% non-resident ownership without a sectoral license.
required_dossiers: GAFI name reservation application form (Form GAFI-OSS-01)
Certified passport copies of all founding quotaholders
Statement of business scope limited to public relations and media consultancy services
Resolution of quotaholders appointing the registration agent, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or public-policy grounds, an alternate name may be re-filed within 24 hours; a formal objection may be lodged with the GAFI Naming Committee within 30 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public (Authar Al-Shahr Al-Aqari) at GAFI OSS notary desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Arabic AOA before the notary; take notarial minutes; verify all quotaholder signatures; pay the notarial stamp duty and obtain the certified notarial duplicate for the GAFI file.
required_dossiers: Draft AOA in Arabic with English transcript
Passport copies and legalized power of attorney if signing by representative
Certificate of name reservation
Quotaholders' resolution on quota apportionment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries transliteration inconsistencies or signatory identity, file a corrected page with marginal notarial endorsement and pay the minor correction fee; rejected drafts are re-submitted with clarified signatures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Capital Deposit and Issuance of Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian commercial bank (e.g., National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr, Commercial International Bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate account using the notarized AOA and quotaholder KYC files; deposit the declared paid-up capital; obtain the bank capital deposit certificate, which must name the LLC and match the AOA capital figure.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarized AOA
Quotaholder identification and KYC/AML declarations
Bank account opening forms and specimen signature cards
Capital deposit certificate request form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further AML clarification, supply a source-of-funds declaration with certified bank statements; if the bank rejects the applicant, transfer the account to another licensed bank or adjust the quota structure via a supplementary quotaholders' resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Submission to the GAFI One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (Cairo headquarters or regional branches)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation application with the notarized AOA, bank deposit certificate, office lease, and name reservation; GAFI coordinates all external approvals and issues the incorporation certificate upon clearance.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation application (Form GAFI-OSS-02)
Three signed originals of the notarized AOA
Bank capital deposit certificate
Office lease contract in the name of the LLC (minimum one-year term)
Name reservation certificate
Government fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query letter, cure comments within 15 working days; if the incorporation is declined, an objection may be submitted to the GAFI Complaints Committee within 30 days; activity-code mismatches are fixed by amending the AOA scope.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Registration and Gazette Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry (under Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade) via GAFI OSS electronic linkage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: GAFI transmits the incorporation file electronically to the Commercial Registry for registration of the LLC; after registry entry, pay the publication fee to the Official Gazette (Al-Waqa'i' Al-Misriyya) and obtain the Commercial Registry extract.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation certificate
Final notarized AOA
Bank certificate confirming the paid-up capital in the corporate account
Office lease and stamp-duty receipts
Publication notice and fee payment voucher
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry flags data inconsistencies, file a rectification statement (Form CR-AM) within 10 working days; registry refusals may be appealed to the Registry Control Committee with the supporting AOA excerpts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the tax card application at the ETA jurisdiction for the registered office; register for VAT with Form ETA-VAT-3 and for withholding purposes; complete NOSI registration for the General Manager, officers, and any employees, filing payroll declarations.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry extract
Certified copy of AOA
Office lease and utility bill
Bank account confirmation and signature cards
Officer and employee ID/passport copies
ETA tax card application and VAT registration forms
NOSI registration forms (Form 1 and Form 2)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: ETA rejection or suspension is cured by correcting e-filing data and resubmitting lease/stamp receipts, or by lodging a statutory objection under the Unified Tax Procedures Law; NOSI discrepancies are resolved by reconciliation filing and payment of arrears.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Civil Defense and Workplace Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil Defense Directorate, Ministry of Interior, and Ministry of Manpower labor office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the office fire-safety inspection application to the Civil Defense Directorate; after physical inspection, obtain the fire safety certificate; separately secure the Ministry of Manpower workplace clearance confirming OHS compliance and social insurance coverage.
required_dossiers: Civil Defense inspection application (Form CD-A1)
Fire extinguisher maintenance contract and inspection invoice
Licensed structural engineer's certification of the office floor plan
OHS program, first-aid equipment list, and evacuation signage layout
NOSI registration confirmation for all officers and employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Inspection deficiencies are cured by installing the required firefighting equipment and re-inspecting within 15 days; a second failure escalates to the Civil Defense technical committee for a structured corrective plan, while Ministry of Manpower objections are appealed with the OHS corrective evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to ISIC 7310 service activity; the only spatial/administrative authority is the district municipal commercial licensing office under Local Administration and GAFI's service licensing window.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Establishment License for Professional Office Activities (Law No. 453 of 1954) – applies solely to the leased office premises and is not a sectoral PR operating license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Category C – administrative office activity under ISIC 7310 generates no industrial pollutants; no EIA scoping, registration, or full report is required under Law No. 4 of 1994 (as amended).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste thresholds apply; general office waste handling must comply with Waste Management Law No. 202 of 2020 (internal segregation, municipal collection contracting); any installed large-format printing equipment must respect Law No. 4/1994 workplace ambient air limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Civil Defense Directorate (Ministry of Interior) requires verified extinguishers, smoke detectors, evacuation signage, and a fire-drill protocol; Ministry of Manpower Workplace Clearance (Form OHS-2) requires an OHS plan, first-aid kit, and NOSI enrollment for staff. Structural load suitability of the leased office is certified by a licensed structural engineer, and the lease must be registered in the LLC's name with the municipal licensing office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) of the Ministry of Finance; unified e-services portal at https://www.eta.gov.eg; mandatory e-invoicing platform at https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign owners incorporate the EG LLC through the GAFI one-stop shop (www.gafi.gov.eg); upon commercial registry activation, the ETA automatically issues a 14-digit Tax Identification Number (TIN) and the Tax Card. VAT registration is completed electronically in the ETA portal once annual taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000 (mandatory), or voluntarily from EGP 50,000; the ETA issues an electronic VAT certificate within 5 working days. Non-resident service providers without an Egyptian permanent establishment are not required to obtain a local TIN; the Egyptian client accounts for reverse-charge VAT and withholding tax under Law 67/2016 Art. 51 and Income Tax Law 91/2005 Art. 56.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The Egyptian-incorporated LLC is a resident taxpayer under Income Tax Law 91/2005 Art. 17 and is taxed at 22.5% on worldwide income; no pass-through is available. Non-resident shareholders are taxed only on Egyptian-source income and distributions. Free-zone / SCZone Tax_Exempt_Zone status is available only by express GAFI licensing and is not a registration default.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt has no check-the-box or hybrid classification election; entity classification follows mandatory statutory rules under the Civil Code and Income Tax Law. Available administrative elections include: (i) depreciation method election; (ii) group loss utilization election under Art. 54 of Law 91/2005; (iii) Investment Law incentive and free-zone election through GAFI; (iv) VAT input-tax allocation method election (direct attribution vs. proportional formula); (v) CFC and transfer-pricing safe-harbor elections under Law 30 of 2023. Hybrid mismatch treatment is statutory only and grants no taxpayer option.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 in annual taxable supplies (mandatory registration threshold); voluntary registration is permitted from EGP 50,000; zero-rated exports to non-residents count toward the threshold, while the Egypt-based PR agency must include all invoices for overseas clients when determining the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time national e-invoicing is fully in force for all VAT-registered entities. Every invoice must be submitted to the ETA e-Invoicing API in bilingual Arabic-English JSON/XML format, digitally signed with an ETA-issued certificate, encoded with a QR stamp, and cleared by the ETA before the supply is deemed legally complete. The e-receipt module is also mandatory for B2C transactions. Non-compliance triggers fines of EGP 100 to EGP 50,000 per invoice, plus TIN suspension for repeated violations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Law 67/2016 Art. 23, exported direct services - including public relations, media relations, and communication consultancy performed by the EG LLC for non-resident clients - qualify for the 0% VAT rate when the following conditions are met: (i) the recipient is a non-resident and the service is contractually and actually performed for overseas use; (ii) the invoice is issued in foreign currency with a clear 'zero-rated export services' statement; (iii) the consideration is received in hard currency through a licensed Egyptian bank within the CBE repatriation window; and (iv) full documentation evidencing offshore performance is retained. The related input VAT on local costs is creditable and refundable through the ETA refund mechanism.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Cargo Release Number on the NAFIZA Single Window) - required only for any physical exports; for services, the NAFIZA export declaration is replaced by the ETA Export Services Declaration
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / CMR (for goods exports) or signed overseas service contract, deliverables, media plans, and campaign performance reports evidencing offshore use (for the PR firm)
Inward Remittance Certificate / CBE foreign-exchange form showing receipt of export proceeds in convertible currency and the matched booking to the export invoice
Original VAT export invoice bearing the zero-rate indicator and QR code, matches with the ETA e-invoicing system
Bank exchange account statement and SWIFT/MT103 evidence of settlement; completion of the Egyptian customs 'Export Accounting' verification
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may retrospectively deny zero-rating and claw back input VAT credits within the 5-year audit window under Law 67/2016 Art. 63. Deficient or fraudulent export substantiation triggers: (i) reassessment at 14% VAT with interest at 2% per month; (ii) administrative fines under Arts. 72-73 ranging from EGP 1,000 to EGP 50,000 per violation and up to EGP 100,000 for invoice integrity breaches; (iii) criminal penalties under Art. 76 including imprisonment up to 5 years and fines of up to 5 times the evaded tax for deliberate falsification; and (iv) automatic inclusion in the CBE non-performing exporter list with suspension of export privileges. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days additionally subjects the exporter to monthly CBE fines up to 2% of the uncollected amount and immediate tax audit escalation under Law 194 of 2020.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — the sole monetary authority and foreign-exchange regulator in Egypt, acting under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020, the Egyptian Exchange Control Law No. 80 of 1947 (as amended), and CBE Foreign-Exchange Department circulars. The CBE licenses all commercial banks, administers the official interbank FX market, receives all mandatory balance-of-payments and export-proceeds reporting, and supervises AML/CFT compliance through the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist-Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Egyptian Pound (EGP) is convertible for permissible current-account transactions, including service fees, management fees, royalties, dividends, and profit repatriation, where the underlying transaction is monetarily genuine and fully documented. Capital-account operations are subject to more intensive bank intermediation: non-resident equity contributions into an Egyptian LLC may enter freely through an authorised bank, but subsequent outward capital repatriation (liquidation distributions, sale of participation, repayment of shareholder loans) must be supported by audited financial statements, evidence of lawful original entry, current tax clearance, and bank records. Egypt operates a bank-intermediated managed float rather than full offshore EGP convertibility; EGP cannot be settled or exchanged outside the authorised banking system meaningfully. For an overseas PR-communication firm, profit remittance is feasible but document-heavy: the LLC must provide audited standalone accounts, a board distribution resolution, proof that the profit is tax-paid, valid commercial registration, and a CBE-compliant direct investment inflow record. Temporary FX liquidity tightness may cause banks to queue high-value remittances, but this is a settlement delay, not a legal prohibition.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For Egyptian resident exporters of services, including cross-border public-relations retainers, the gross invoice proceeds must be repatriated through an authorised Egyptian bank. Under prevailing CBE export-proceeds practice, the foreign exchange must be received by the bank within 90 calendar days from the service invoice due date, unless the bank agrees to a documented extension for valid commercial reasons. Once received, the funds must be posted to a designated foreign-currency collection/retention account or converted into EGP at the interbank market price. A mandatory 100% conversion presumption applies in the absence of a CBE-recognised foreign-currency expenditure plan; the entity may lower the conversion requirement to zero by submitting a rolling foreign-currency cash-flow forecast covering overseas subcontractors, media placements, cloud/subscription fees, and other genuine external liabilities. Every service export must be accompanied by an electronic declaration in the bank’s export system, the signed PR service contract, purchase order, performance statement, and the correct CBE balance-of-payments purpose code for business/public-relations services. Late collection, split-receipting, or the use of an unlicensed offshore payment intermediary to settle the proceeds directly into EGP outside the banking system would constitute a breach of Egyptian exchange-control rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EGP) plus USD current-account ledger; usable for export-proceeds retention and profit-remittance clearance; no separate statutory capital-escrow account is mandatory for LLCs.
Operational EGP account, USD/LIBOR-denominated settlement account, and export-proceeds collection sub-account.
Operational multi-currency account (EGP/USD/EUR) with dedicated corporate e-banking, SWIFT payment, and FX-hedging capacity.
Cross-border operational account with direct SWIFT MT103/MT202 coverage via HSBC group correspondent network; ideal for overseas media-client collections.
Operational EGP/USD account with documentary trade and letter-of-credit handling capacity.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW. Egypt does not recognise foreign electronic-money institutions or digital-only cross-border banks as settlement banks for resident corporate accounts. Wise, Revolut, Payoneer, and similar offshore EMIs may be used strictly as front-end collection/payment tools, but all statutory service export proceeds must be swept into an authorised Egyptian bank account before EGP conversion or any CBE-compliant disbursement. No passporting or EMI equivalence regime exists in Egypt; an offshore EMI cannot issue a CBE-recognised export proceeds receipt and cannot satisfy the physical corporate-KYC mandate. Locally licensed payment fintech companies in Egypt operate under CBE e-payment licences and still require a settlement account at a licensed bank; they do not replace commercial banking rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory. At least one Egyptian-lawfully-authorized director/manager and each natural-person beneficial owner, or a formally appointed attorney-in-fact with a notarised and Apostilled/MFA-legalised power of attorney, must attend an initial face-to-face KYC interview at the branch. Fully remote account opening for non-resident corporate shareholders is not accepted by Egyptian banks under standard CBE CDD rules; the CBE permits e-KYC primarily for certain Egyptian natural persons and never for complex legal entities. The LLC must present its commercial registration certificate, GAFI investment file, tax card, articles of association, board resolution on bank account signatories, proof of registered office, passports of UBOs, source-of-funds declaration, and Arabic translations of all non-Arabic documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial-ownership chain above the Egyptian LLC, particularly overseas holding vehicles in low-tax, non-transparent jurisdictions used by a global PR group; the bank cannot complete a standard 'know-your-UBO' review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the full group ownership chart showing each intermediate legal entity and percentage interest through to every natural-person UBO above 10%; certified register of beneficial owners; passports of all natural-person UBOs; board resolutions of each intermediate holding vehicle; notarised source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements explaining the Egyptian equity contribution; legal opinion from Egyptian counsel confirming absence of shell/undisclosed-nominee risk; and a written undertaking to update the bank and CBE ownership records annually.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transfer-pricing red flag because the main payor is an affiliated overseas media or advertising entity; invoiced retainers may appear over-stated in relation to services performed in Egypt.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the full overseas main service contract and each campaign work-order; monthly service reports and content/crisis-response deliverables; activity and milestone evidence such as press materials, media placement schedules, public-relations campaign calendars; a transfer-pricing benchmarking memorandum using an uncontrolled service price or cost-plus approach for PR services; the Egyptian LLC’s audited management accounts; the client-side advertising budget approval; and corporate email/project-management records demonstrating genuine commercial substance and a clear correlation between invoiced amounts and delivered services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party or non-counterparty remitters sending retainer payments; the bank flags a payment-chain mismatch because the named external PR client is not the remitter.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Create and submit a remitter-versus-client linkage file: for each remitter, a commercial-register excerpt, UBO confirmation, and explanation of the agency/billing relationship; a legally signed debtor/creditor or payment-authorisation declaration from the original client directing the payment; the consolidated campaign payment schedule; board affidavit from EG_LLC confirming no undisclosed nominee or conduit arrangement; enhanced due-diligence notes on the remitter’s jurisdiction; and no-objection correspondence from the final client.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/embargo exposure due to PR work for state-owned media, government-controlled advertisers, or entities partially operating in high-risk or restricted jurisdictions, causing funds to be blocked on compliance grounds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce a sanctions-screening report for the client, its shareholders and ultimate media beneficiaries showing negative hits on UN/EU/US OFAC/UK HMT and Egyptian CBE restricted-party lists; signed anti-terrorism and anti-sanctions warranties from the client and the end-advertiser; description of the PR services confirming no prohibited advertising or arms/defence-related content; detailed allocation of each funds flow and campaign purpose; legal opinion on the lawfulness of the engagement under both Egyptian law and international secondary sanctions; and an agreement to reject, unwind, or repatriate any payment appearing after negative news screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment settlement routed through offshore EMI, prepaid card, cryptocurrency wallet, or a third-party gateway, which the bank perceives as an attempt to circumvent Egypt’s export-proceeds and surrender rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present a bank treasury-side attestation that the Egyptian USD/EGP collection account is the contractual settlement account; provide gateway and EMI statements demonstrating that enterprising funds are automatically or daily swept into the authorised Egyptian bank before any EGP conversion; reconcile every invoice to a unique wire reference and purpose code; file the required CBE export-proceeds declarations showing full repatriation; execute a compliance memorandum committing that no crypto-currency or shell payment mechanism will be used; and supply the bank with a copy of the negative-screening report for the EMI provider.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant route for a foreign shareholder injecting equity into EG_LLC is a direct SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder’s bank account to the LLC’s USD/EUR account held at an authorised Egyptian bank. The wire must name the beneficiary as EG_LLC, contain the shareholder legal name in field 50, and use a clear remittance reference such as 'FDI-EQ-CAP-EG-LLC' or a GAFI investment-file reference. The receiving bank will assign the transaction the CBE statistical/BOP purpose code for direct investment equity capital (commonly 'Direct Investment – Share Capital into an Egyptian Resident Company'; the exact statistical code is selected in the bank’s E-boarding system). the bank enters the inflow into the CBE’s external investment and capital position recording; if the contribution is made in USD and the LLC requires EGP operating capital, the bank converts the funds at the interbank rate through the Egypt Electronic Foreign Exchange System (EFES) and issues a capital-inflow certificate. Supporting documents for verification include the LLC’s constitutional documents, GAFI incorporation/amendment certificate, non-resident shareholder board resolution, source of funds, passport copies, and compliance declarations. The capital must be used only for the LLC’s stated corporate purposes, not for speculative FX positions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For overseas trade and service payments, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for direct credit to a nominated beneficiary, with an optional MT202 COVER where the bank settles through a correspondent. For high-value or documentary transactions, the LLC may open an irrevocable commercial Letter of Credit (LC) confirmed by a reputable international bank, transmitted by SWIFT MT700/MT710 subject to UCP600. The outbound remitting bank must receive an underlying invoice, contract, service completion evidence, and the correct CBE payment purpose code; disbursements can be funded either from the LLC’s retained foreign-currency export-proceeds account or by purchasing EGP for USD at the prevailing market rate. Where the payment is to the entity’s own overseas affiliate, an additional transfer-pricing file must be maintained to support the amount and timing. All outbound wires should be pre-screened through the bank’s sanctions filter and comply with Egypt’s anti-money-laundering reporting thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/EGP forward contract with an authorised Egyptian bank, concluded only for an actual or anticipated retainer-receivable or operating-payable exposure and carrying strict non-speculative documentation; settlement occurs at maturity through the EFES rate with physical EGP delivery.

Onshore FX swap (swap-in/swap-out of USD and EGP) with a licensed bank, used for temporary liquidity alignment between a foreign-currency receipt and an imminent EGP expenditure, executed as two matched legs with a zero or transparent spread.

Cross-currency swap between USD and EGP with an authorised bank, used to hedge balance-sheet exposures arising from a long-term foreign-currency shareholder loan or multi-year overseas retainer contract, with periodic net payments matched to the underlying cash-flow profile.

Zero-cost collar / range forward involving USD and EGP, available on a relationship-approved treasury basis to cap conversion cost and set a floor for expected export-proceeds conversions, supported by audited receivables forecasts and CBE-compliant underlying documentation.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) in EGP/USD is not generally permissible for the Egyptian resident LLC onshore; it may be considered only where the Egyptian bank and CBE provide an explicit exception, typically for a non-resident affiliate or where the hedging need cannot be settled in EGP; as a rule, the LLC should avoid NDFs unless CBE clearance in writing is obtained.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual auditors' report, managers' report, and approved annual financial statements for the Egyptian limited liability company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the end of the fiscal year; approved minutes and financial statements must be filed with GAFI within 30 days after the partners' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the audited financial statements and minutes triggers GAFI administrative warning letters, statutory late-filing fines, and after three consecutive years of non-filing can lead to administrative strike-off of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return with accompanying audited financial statements and required tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Corporate Income Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the fiscal year end; for a 31 December fiscal year, the return is due by 30 April, subject to the available e-filing extension through a licensed tax accountant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and late payment interest are computed at the statutory Egyptian Tax Authority rate per month, plus a minimum late-filing penalty; prolonged failure to file may trigger enforced tax collection, cancellation of the tax card, and administrative reference for commercial registry strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial registry renewal declaration and principal officer confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office of the competent Governorate / GAFI unified registration window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for calendar-year natural trailing period, or within 30 days after the company's registered anniversary date, depending on the regime applied to the LLC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unrenewed commercial registration is administratively suspended; continued omission attracts a statutory monetary fine and may result in deletion from the Commercial Registry and subsequent administrative strike-off of the LLC.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership register confirmation and supporting partner register update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Unit (EMLCU) and GAFI through the licensed corporate agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At the time of the annual commercial registry renewal and within 30 days of any transfer of quotas or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-maintenance or false filing of the UBO register carries administrative fines under the Egyptian AML legislation for legal persons, liability of directors and managers, and repeated violations may support administrative deregistration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold applies: every Egyptian LLC must appoint at least one Egyptian licensed statutory auditor and have its annual financial statements audited before submission to the partners' meeting and GAFI, unless a specific statutory exemption in the Companies Law applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which are aligned with IFRS; listed or large entities adopt full IFRS-converged EAS, while qualifying small and medium LLCs may apply the EAS special provisions for SMEs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC's managers must confirm the current ultimate beneficial owners, owners of 25% or more of the quotas, and those exercising control at each annual partners' meeting; any quota transfer is recognized in the Register of Partners and reported to GAFI and the EMLCU within 30 days, and the annual UBO confirmation must accompany the commercial registry renewal.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 - 1,200 per annum for registered office address, local corporate agent, and annual notification services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,000 - 2,800 per annum for a small overseas PR communication LLC depending on transaction volume, register complexity, and bank account activity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% (flat rate for all resident juridical persons under Law No. 30 of 2023 on Income Tax; the pre-2023 bifurcated regime — 22.5% for listed companies and 25% for unlisted companies — has been unified for tax periods commencing on or after January 1, 2024).
